This perspective motivates a program of \emph{natural mathematics}, by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition. Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.

papers.title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
papers.abstract: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-{\mu}m to 30 {\mu}m and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

papers.title: Burning the Bridge: Agentification and Domestic Value Added
papers.abstract: Firms that replace local work with foreign AI agents can produce more per paid hour while generating less income at home. We study this trade-off in a small open economy where exporters and local services both use agents. Once wages reach a reservation floor, extending agent use in local services lowers domestic income at unchanged foreign costs. Value added at constant prices and consumption also fall if suppliers capture enough of the saving. Exporters have an offset: adopting agents can expand production and earn the foreign exchange needed to pay for them. The difference is substantial. Using Brazilian accounts as a reference, a supplier bargaining share above about 0.15 is sufficient to make further local-service adoption reduce value added even at negligible foreign costs. The corresponding threshold in tradables is about 0.66. We derive separate export-growth requirements for preserving income and consumption and illustrate them using historical accounts for Brazil and Mexico. Cheaper agents ease the consumption requirement; lower export prices raise it. Over time, declining domestic capabilities can also make returning to local production more expensive, allowing suppliers to charge more at renewal.

papers.title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
papers.abstract: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing deployment for DOE science missions. This Blueprint proposes that DOE focus on (1) deploying first-generation scientifically relevant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits and performing at least 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations in scientifically relevant calculations; (2) developing essential FTQC programming competencies, system software, and facility readiness; and (3) investing in cutting-edge focused R&D that fosters breakthroughs in scientific applications, algorithms, and logical architectures needed to accelerate the advent of scientific utility. This effort will position DOE to transition to larger systems: production-scale quantum computers that comprise 1,000 to 10,000 logical qubits, perform 1 to 10 billion hard logical operations, and execute scientifically useful computations at scale. The Blueprint calls for transformative R&D and collective action to accelerate the advent of scientific quantum utility and bring it within reach by 2028.

papers.title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
papers.abstract: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

papers.title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
papers.abstract: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$ when $\mu$ is obtained from $\lambda$ by adding one to a part of $\lambda$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ and $\mathcal{S}^\mu$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $\lambda$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^\lambda$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^\lambda$ to $\mathcal{S}^{\lambda'}$.

papers.title: An easy proof of transience of one-dimensional Rademacher walk with power weights
papers.abstract: Using a version of a local limit theorem, we provide an easy proof that the Rademacher random walk with step sizes $n^\alpha$, $\alpha>1/2$, is transient.

papers.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
papers.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, André, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes
papers.abstract: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.

papers.title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and Néel temperature
papers.abstract: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the Néel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

papers.title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
papers.abstract: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

papers.title: Imaging Compressible and Incompressible Kinetic Energy of a 2d Bose-Einstein Condensate
papers.abstract: We introduce a method based on velocity-sensitive two-photon transitions to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field as well as the local atomic density of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a single realization. We quantitatively benchmark the method on a quantized vortex. Applied to a condensate far from equilibrium, the method reveals the contrasting behaviors of the system's flow kinetic energy components, where the compressible component quickly decays while the incompressible one remains, dominating the long-time dynamics.

papers.title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
papers.abstract: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.

papers.title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
papers.abstract: We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.

papers.title: Dispersive estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for limit-periodic operators that are super-exponentially well-approximated by periodic operators. The key ingredient is a sharp enhanced convexity statement for the density of states of periodic Jacobi matrices. This statement implies log-convexity of the density of states and hence is a strengthening of existing results on the convexity of equilibrium measures. We expect that it will be of interest and use outside of this work. We also construct almost-periodic discrete Schrödinger operators with purely singular continuous spectrum whose unitary groups enjoy recurrent dispersive motion: on one subsequence of time scales, the unitary group has a dispersive estimate at a rate as close to the free rate as one desires, while on another set of time scales, the unitary group is as far from dispersive as possible. In fact, this behavior is generic within the class of limit-periodic operators.

papers.title: Learning to find cosmic filaments with graph neural networks
papers.abstract: Inferring the large-scale structure of the Universe from galaxy surveys is a fundamental challenge in cosmology. In particular, cosmic filaments form an extended and geometrically complex network whose underlying structure cannot be reconstructed from discrete galaxy catalogs without uncertainty. We investigate a generative approach to filament finding based on flow matching and graph neural networks. The learned model reproduces key statistical properties of the target filament distribution while generating a distribution over possible filament configurations, demonstrating its ability to model uncertainty. Our work provides a first step towards probabilistic inference of the cosmic web directly from galaxy surveys. More broadly, these results demonstrate the potential of conditional generative models for reconstructing filament-like structures from sparse observational tracers.

papers.title: Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
papers.abstract: We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Korányi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $\Omega \setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $ u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partial\Omega, \quad u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, then $\Omega$ must itself be a Korányi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it is an affine normalization of the fundamental solution of $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$.

papers.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity
papers.abstract: Spatial arbitrage pricing theory (S-APT) extends factor models to allow returns to spill over between connected firms, beyond what common risk factors explain. In recent years, tabular foundation models (TFMs) have matched or outperformed tuned gradient-boosted and bagged ensembles on small and medium-sized tabular benchmarks. Although their predictive performance is strong, these models reveal little about what they have learned, which limits their use in regulated financial applications that require explanation. Internal representations are widely used to probe what neural networks learn and to measure similarity. In this paper, we use the frozen representations of four TFMs as a measure of financial dissimilarity in a spatial asset-pricing model of US equities from 2011 to 2025, and find that their estimated gains over a direct distance between the same disclosures become consistently positive once broad SEC filing data are included. This reframes tabular foundation models from black-box predictors into instruments for measuring economic structure, with immediate applications to peer selection, risk attribution and network-based asset pricing. More broadly, our findings suggest that the internal representations of foundation models, not only their predictions, deserve study as economic objects, opening a new line of research on what pretrained models know about firms.

papers.title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
papers.abstract: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gouëzel skew products [Gouëzel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.

papers.title: Higher-symmetry selection rules for second- and third-harmonic radiation in the Bullough-Dodd model
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear excitations of the discrete shape mode about a static complex soliton of the integrable Bullough-Dodd model. Extending the linear stability analysis to third order in the excitation amplitude, we construct explicit spatially localised corrections to the shape-mode oscillation and determine its nonlinear frequency shift using the Poincaré-Lindstedt method. Although both the second and third harmonics lie inside the continuous spectrum of the linearised fluctuation operator, the corresponding inhomogeneous equations admit exact localised particular solutions. We demonstrate that the nonlinear sources have vanishing on-shell overlaps with the scattering states at both harmonic frequencies, suppressing the corresponding radiative responses. We further investigate the role of integrability and show how a higher commuting symmetry of the Bullough-Dodd equation provides a perturbative selection-rule interpretation of these cancellations. Our results illustrate how higher integrable symmetries can constrain nonlinear resonances that are otherwise permitted by the linear spectrum.

papers.title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
papers.abstract: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.

papers.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
papers.abstract: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.

papers.title: Generalized Images and Multi-Index Transmutations for Brownian First Passage to Polynomial Boundaries
papers.abstract:
We study Brownian first passage to a finite polynomial boundary \[ F(t)=d+\sum_{j=2}^p c_jt^j. \] For every such boundary we construct a time-independent signed exterior image measure. Consequently, on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian scale, its heat potential is the killed transition kernel and its boundary flux is the first-passage density. For $F(t)=At^2+Bt^3$ we also derive fifth- and eighth-order scalar annihilators and prove their exact rational factorization. Numerical experiments for two- and three-term polynomial boundaries independently agree with Durbin's equation to discretization accuracy.

papers.title: Single-shot on-chip measurement of the modal Stokes parameters
papers.abstract: Integrated photonics has recently facilitated manipulating multimode partially coherent light in a compact mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers. A critical task in this context is on-chip reconstruction of the coherence matrix through a sequence of measurement configurations, thus giving rise to a speed bottleneck stemming from temporal delays in tuning on-chip phase shifts. Here we demonstrate single-shot reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light by parallelizing the on-chip measurements of the modal Stokes parameters, thereby exchanging space for time. Although a larger chip area is required, the reconstruction is limited only by detection speed, thus potentially paving the way to real-time reconstruction of coherence matrices for applications in high-speed communications, cryptography, computation, and sensing.

papers.title: Transferable, Time-Parallel Graph Dynamics via Space-Time Factorization
papers.abstract: Time-parallel neural operators (FNO and successors) have transformed PDE surrogates on regular grids. Mesh-based operators (MeshGraphNets, Transolver) extend operator learning to irregular geometries, but jointly learning across diverse topologies while retaining non-recurrent temporal evaluation remains challenging. We propose space-time factorization: partition the model into local temporal operators (learned, graph-independent) and a spatial mixer that propagates information across nodes without graph-dependent learned parameters. This structural condition lets the same parameters run on unseen graphs; non-recurrent instances also admit time-parallel evaluation. Accurate zero-shot transfer further depends on controlling three information leaks (graph-dependent weights, graph-specific features, and graph-correlated training distributions) and on suitable task physics and training coverage. The protocol applies to two distinct spatial-mixer families, fixed-spectral and learned-attention. We validate the principle in three domains. For floodwave propagation in river networks, a 27K-parameter model trained on the Yangtze transfers zero-shot to the Mississippi with median NSE 0.998 in boundary-conditioned operational evaluation, training 5.5x faster than a stabilized recurrent baseline. On cross-geometry Navier-Stokes, the three-seed SepFNO mean relative vorticity error on five unseen targets falls by about 28% from 5 to 12 training geometries, with a consistent single-run SepTransolver trend. On cross-city traffic forecasting, zero-shot transfer reaches within 12.9% of an oracle trained on the target city. Across settings, cross-geometry error decreases with both the number of training geometries and their relatedness to the test, at a rate depending on the spatial mixer. This opens the path to pooled-data, foundation-style models for graph dynamics on irregular topologies.

papers.title: Long-range effective interactions in a rectangular tight-binding lattice within the semiclassical approximation
papers.abstract: We extend the semiclassical formalism of Dunlap--Kenkre (1986) and of Mamani et al. (2017) to obtain the effective Hamiltonian of a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, in the presence of a rapidly oscillating field $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ and a static potential $V(x,y)$, both arbitrary, by means of: a canonical transformation, the semiclassical approximation and the Kapitza-type time-averaging techniques (Mamani 2017). At zeroth order in $1/\omega$, a field with even symmetry reparameterizes the hopping elements through factors in terms of Bessel functions. At order $1/\omega^2$, the induced hopping elements arise from the coupling between the oscillating field and the curvature of the static potential (its 2nd derivative). For fields $\mathbf f(\omega t)$ with odd symmetry, in addition to renormalizing the interactions, an effective band shift appears. For the two-dimensional lattice, we obtain the generalization of the exact dynamic localization condition of Dignam et al. (2002) and Domachuk et al. (2002), and we show that the resulting band-collapse is in general anisotropic --axial interactions are suppressed but some diagonal interactions persist--, so that exact dynamic localization in the stroboscopic sense is guaranteed only when the band-collapse is complete for all neighbors. Finally, we numerically identify an effective-duplication scenario for the rectangular lattice, associated with approximate solutions of a Pythagorean-type relation among zeros of the zeroth-order Bessel function.

papers.title: Convergence rate of rescaled mean curvature flows over asymptotically conical shrinkers
papers.abstract: We study how rapidly a rescaled mean curvature flow can approach an asymptotically conical self-shrinker. For a global normal graph with small $C^1$ norm and time-integrable $C^0$ norm, we prove that every nonzero solution has a leading asymptotic term given by an eigenfunction of the linearized operator $L$. In particular, a global graph $u$ with $e^{kt}\|u\|_{C^1}\to 0$ for every $k$ must coincide with the shrinker. We also construct a nonzero local graph over an immersed asymptotically conical shrinker with $C^2$ super-exponential decay in every bounded subset. This flow is defined on expanding open graphical domains. The example illustrates how rigidity fails in the local graphical setting.

papers.title: Uniqueness Results for Static Asymptotically Locally Hyperbolic (ALH) Manifolds
papers.abstract: We give uniqueness results for related classes of static asymptotically locally hyperbolic (ALH) manifolds. As an application, we give examples of one ended hyperbolic manifolds with boundary that are not optimal for the Positive Mass Theorem or for the Riemannian Penrose Inequality

papers.title: Matrix Criteria for Mordell--Weil Ranks of Quartic Twists of $y^2=x^3+x$ with Root Number $-1$
papers.abstract: We study the Mordell--Weil ranks of quartic twists $E_a:y^2=x^3+ax$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with global root number $-1$. For $D$ a product of $n\ge2$ distinct odd primes, a $2$-isogeny descent yields unconditional rank bounds for $E_D$, $E_{-D}$, and $E_{-2D}$ in terms of matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by additive Legendre symbols. Under suitable congruence and matrix-rank conditions, these curves have rank at most one, and rank one assuming the Mordell--Weil parity conjecture. For $E_{-2D}$, an additional explicit square condition establishes rank one unconditionally. Our results extend earlier two-prime criteria to arbitrary numbers of prime factors and further to fourth-power-free coefficients $H=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i^{e_i}$, where $e_i\in\{1,3\}$.

papers.title: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $\Pi_1^0$ statements about $\zeta(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, Gödel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. The self-referential result converts a digital encoding framework with any uniform proof-compression principle for RH into an immediate non-constructive refutation of RH. Given that, with human input and computer assistance, $\mathsf{RH}$ has been formally verified in the Lean theorem prover strictly within constructive logic, this contradiction does not refute $\mathsf{RH}$. Instead, it falsifies $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$. We conclude by isolating the exact proof-theoretic obstruction---Pudlák's lower bound on bounded reflection proofs---showing why the analytic regularity of $\mathsf{RH}$ cannot compress logical self-reference, and exposing the limits of applying the Law of Excluded Middle to uncomputably bounded searches.

papers.title: The Jupiter ICy moons Explorer (JUICE) Mission: Post-Launch Status and Mission Overview
papers.abstract: The JUpiter ICy Moons Explorer (JUICE) is the first large-class mission in ESA's Cosmic Vision programme. Proposed in 2007 and selected in 2012, it was launched on 14 April 2023 from Kourou and is now en route towards Jupiter. After arrival in July 2031, JUICE will spend approximately four years studying the Jupiter system, performing multiple flybys of three of its Galilean moons, the icy moons Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto, before entering orbit around Ganymede for its final year. The mission will investigate conditions that may support habitable environments within the satellites, all of which are thought to contain subsurface liquid water oceans. Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System, is a prime target due to its internal structure and possible subsurface ocean, its unique intrinsic magnetic field, and its complex interactions with Jupiter's magnetosphere, offering a natural laboratory for studying the emergence, evolution and potential habitability of icy worlds around giant planets. JUICE will also conduct a global investigation of the Jupiter system as the archetype for gaseous giant planet systems: it will study Jupiter's atmospheric circulation, composition, and flow of energy from the cloud tops to the thermosphere and characterise the 3D structure of the magnetosphere and its coupling with the ionosphere and thermosphere. Interactions between the moons and the magnetosphere, as well as tidal and gravitational evolution within the Galilean system, will also be assessed. Additional science objectives include the innermost Galilean moon, Io and its neutral cloud and plasma torus, some small inner and irregular moons, and the ring systems. The payload includes 10 instruments and one experiment using the spacecraft's telecommunications system to connect with ground-based radio telescopes, plus an onboard radiation monitor.

papers.title: Geometric Control Analysis of an Internally Actuated Flying Wing
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous geometric accessibility and controllability analysis for a fixed-wing Uncrewed Aircraft System (UAS) actuated solely by an internal moving mass, a momentum wheel, and external thrust. This configuration eliminates traditional control surfaces, which in turn reduces the combinatorial set of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies necessary for high-fidelity modeling of flight through unsteady flow fields. Using Lie bracket computations and the strong Lie Algebra Rank Condition, it is shown that the full nonlinear dynamics are generically small-time locally accessible, with singular configurations explicitly characterized and shown to be immediately escapable by direct mass actuation. The stronger property of small-time local controllability is shown to hold for the attitude subsystem at equilibrium points, using Sussmann's condition. A key contribution is the explicit treatment of the time-varying inertia tensor via the Huygens-Steiner Theorem, which introduces nontrivial coupling between the control vector fields. The momentum wheel provides direct yaw authority that, combined with inertia variation from the moving mass, generates a full-rank accessibility Lie algebra. A nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (MPC) is derived with consideration of flight envelope constraints and is applied to track different trajectories under unperturbed and perturbed flow field conditions.

papers.title: Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.

papers.title: The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability
papers.abstract: The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $\Delta$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $\Delta^2E_b$, and below $E=\Delta^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $\Delta$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2\Delta}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\gg\Delta^2E_b$. The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2\Delta}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.

papers.title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
papers.abstract: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

papers.title: An exact and fast solution for the common overlap of three disks in mutual transits and eclipses
papers.abstract: The area common to three disks determines how much light is blocked during mutual events of transiting planets, moons, and eclipsing multiple stars. We present a new solution that removes every case distinction from the evaluation and corrects several errors in earlier work. We prove that a non-degenerate overlap has at most four corners, which reduces the geometry to five topologies that a single directed walk along the boundary arcs resolves. Green's theorem then yields the area as a sum of circular segments and a vertex polygon. The evaluation needs one arctangent per arc, suffers no subtractive cancellation, and handles arcs longer than $\pi$ without a special case. We verify the solution for all cases and show that the algorithm is componentwise backward stable. Five public packages that compute the same area fail on some of our test configurations, either through undefined values, missing topologies, or lost precision. Our complete computation takes 45 ns per configuration on one CPU core, which is four to several thousand times faster than the public packages. The same decomposition also delivers the centroid of the overlap in closed form.

papers.title: Gluon GPDs from hard-exclusive electroproduction of heavy quarkonium at NLO
Dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion via sharp large deviations
papers.abstract: We prove a dynamical phase transition in Brownian motion with drift, a phenomenon recently predicted in the physics literature. Specifically, when a Brownian motion with drift on a long time interval is conditioned on an upper large deviation event for the (normalized) occupation measure of the interval [-1,1], in the spirit of the Gibbs conditioning principle, a phase transition occurs. If one conditions on a large deviation event in the far upper tail, the conditioned process follows the Langevin diffusion suggested by the Donsker-Varadhan variational formula for additive functionals. In contrast, if one conditions on a large deviation event in the near upper tail, the conditioned process follows a different Langevin diffusion on a fraction of the time interval and subsequently behaves like the unconditioned process. We establish this phase transition via a new sharp large deviation result for the occupation measure, which is of independent interest. We also provide further corollaries of this result and discuss generalizations to other Markov processes and additive functionals.

papers.title: A multimodal foundation model for tissue proteomics and morphology in cancer
Symbolic Regression Diagnostics of 1D Lyman Alpha Forest Emulator
papers.abstract: We use symbolic regression to diagnose the parameter dependence of a black-box multi-fidelity emulator of the Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum. Symbolic regression is appealing in its ability to reduce complex parameter spaces, thereby reducing compute time and offering potential interpretability in parameter inter-dependencies. Starting from a pretrained Gaussian-process (GP) emulator that connects low- and high-resolution PRIYA simulations, we search for explicit equations describing the dependence of the power spectrum on resolution and each cosmological and astrophysical parameter. We find that symbolic regression can recover equations that reproduce the emulator values well, but accurate predictions do not guarantee accurate parameter derivatives, making such equations unreliable for downstream applications such as Fisher forecasts. We therefore introduce a derivative-faithfulness diagnostic that directly compares the parameter gradient of each symbolic equation to the GP, and explore a derivative-matching (Sobolev) loss to improve this agreement. At z = 3.6, the Sobolev objective yields derivative-faithful equations for 9 of the 11 PRIYA parameters constraining the Lyman-alpha forest, with the approach only ineffective on h and AGN, whose 1D power spectrum imprints are weak or degenerate. Redefining the training objective with the Sobolev loss is a more robust and computationally efficient approach to gradient-matching repair than increasing model complexity. Our methods present potential mitigation strategies for failure modes of PySR, enabling downstream Fisher forecasts in some of these cases. Further, we document limitations potentially relevant to future work bridging symbolic regression with emulators. Our results demonstrate symbolic regression as an emulator diagnostic tool, with particular utility for low-dimensional or weakly coupled parameter dependencies.

papers.title: Critical ocean physics on the edge of AMOC instability
papers.abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is expected to weaken under global warming, but whether this signifies a transient response or a tipping transition remains unclear. Distinguishing between these cases requires a physical understanding of the boundary separating ocean states leading to AMOC recovery from those leading to collapse. In a global ocean model with 1° resolution, we compute an AMOC edge state -- an unstable saddle equilibrium that anchors this instability boundary. The edge state maintains weak overturning sourced by marginal deep water formation in the Nordic Seas. Analyzing the North Atlantic freshwater and heat balances that govern the edge state dynamics, we show that near the edge state, thermal and haline components of the surface buoyancy flux approximately compensate. Surface buoyancy loss (gain) coincides with AMOC recovery (collapse). Our findings support using the regional net surface buoyancy flux as an indicator for the onset of AMOC tipping.

papers.title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
papers.abstract: Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carathéodory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[ d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2 =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

papers.title: Learning from Human Corrections through Temporal Preferences
Quarkonium Energy Correlators in Proton-Proton Collisions: Analytic Calculation and Angular-Momentum Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We present the first complete leading-order (LO) analytic calculation of the quarkonium energy correlator (QEC) in $pp$ collisions, for the color-singlet ${}^3S_1^{[1]}$ and the color-octet ${}^1S_0^{[8]}$, ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$, and ${}^3P_J^{[8]}$ channels of $J/\psi$ production. Instead of the high-$p_T$ fragmentation approximation, the calculation retains the full kinematics of the recoil parton, inverts the map from transverse momentum to the rest-frame angle in closed form, and is validated by \textsc{HELAC-onia} in shape and absolute normalization. We also give the analytic counterpart of the $p_T$-weighted variant of the correlator. The LO shape of each channel is organized by the total angular momentum $J$ of the $c\bar c$ pair, as a consequence of the tree-level selection rule that forbids two on-shell gluons from forming a $J=1$ state. This hierarchy is compressed in the central sPHENIX acceptance and exposed by the wider forward coverage at the LHC. In the distribution normalized to the total cross section, much though not all of the scale uncertainty cancels, leaving promising distinctions in the QEC shapes between different $J/\psi$ production channels. The discriminating power of the QEC can be further improved by next-to-leading-order calculations and by utilizing QECs in simultaneous fits with the $p_T$ spectrum and polarization measurements.

papers.title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
papers.abstract: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.

papers.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

papers.title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
Constraining the Leptonic and Hadronic Contributions to the Gamma-Ray Emission of SNR HESS J1731-347 with CTAO Forecasts
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian broadband spectral analysis of the supernova remnant HESS J1731-347, combining archival radio, X-ray, and H.E.S.S. data with a new analysis of 16 yr of Fermi-LAT observations. The LAT data allow the GeV emission of the western molecular-cloud core (MC-core) to be separated from that of the remaining shell. We fit purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models with and without the MC-core region. Within a one-zone model with fixed distance and ambient density, the lepto-hadronic scenario is strongly preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) in both cases. Excluding the MC-core, we obtain $\Delta{\rm BIC}=33.67$, a magnetic field of $B = 84.9^{+27.5}_{-22.9}$ $\mu$G, a hard proton index of $\alpha_p = 1.69 \pm 0.10$, and a proton energy of $W_p = (4.37^{+0.64}_{-0.51})\times10^{48}$ erg for $n_{\rm H}=20$ cm$^{-3}$. The preference for a hadronic contribution is therefore not driven by the MC-core emission alone. CTAO simulations show that a 50 h observation with the southern array would detect the source at $13\sigma$ to $18\sigma$ and substantially improve the constraints on its TeV spectrum.

papers.title: Directed brain-body graphs across timescales
Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
Split Ends: UV Physics branches Black Hole Hair
papers.abstract: Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs. Moreover, BHs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. This branching has profound consequences for BH physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves.

papers.title: Which Ellipses Are Outlines of a Given Ellipsoid? A Ratio Test with Unknown Focal Length
Is 4 Bits Enough for EEG Sleep Staging? A Subject-Level Benchmark of MXFP4, NVFP4 and FP8
Tornado4D: Physics-Guided 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of a Laboratory Tornado from Sparse One-Sided Videos
The Recycler: In-Transit Machine Learning on High-Fidelity Data from Simulation Campaigns as an Optimized Approach for Building Frontier Models
Topological Phase Transition of $ F_{α}{}^{γ} F^{αβ} F_{β}{}^{η} \ F^{λμ} R_{γηλμ} $ AdS Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic criticality and topological properties of four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter black holes in the presence of a nonminimal electromagnetic-curvature interaction of the form \(F_{\alpha}{}^{\gamma}F^{\alpha\beta}F_{\beta}{}^{\eta}F^{\lambda\mu}R_{\gamma\eta\lambda\mu}\). Treating the coupling perturbatively to first order, we construct the corrected black hole solutions and derive their thermodynamic quantities in the extended phase space. Conventional critical behavior is examined through the criticality conditions for the Hawking temperature in both canonical and grand canonical ensembles. We then use thermodynamic topology to investigate the global structure of equilibrium configurations and its dependence on the thermodynamic parameters. In the canonical ensemble, two distinct regimes emerge: a noncritical region characterized by a total winding number \(W=+1\), and a critical region with \(W=0\). In the grand canonical ensemble, three distinct regimes are identified according to the electric potential. Interestingly, the low- and intermediate-potential regions share the same topological number, \(W=+1\), although conventional critical points occur only in the intermediate-potential region. The high-potential region, by contrast, is characterized by \(W=0\) and exhibits no conventional critical behavior. Our findings show that thermodynamic topology provides a global characterization of equilibrium configurations that complements conventional temperature-based criticality analysis, and that the global winding number alone does not uniquely determine the existence of conventional critical points.

papers.title: Current-Dependent Meta-GGA and Local Hybrid Functionals for Relativistic NMR Shifts
papers.abstract: NMR chemical shifts are key for the characterization of novel compounds. Especially for molecules with heavy elements, the experimental data is often corroborated with computational studies in density functional theory (DFT). However, modern meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) and local hybrid functionals are not widely supported in relativistic calculations with quantum chemistry program suites. So far, their current-dependent generalization in the spirit of Dobson, Becke, and Tao was not presented at all. This generalization ensures gauge invariance and does not introduce artifacts--unlike the more popular field-dependent generalization of the kinetic-energy density. In non-relativistic and scalar-relativistic calculations, the first was shown to be superior but the current density only arises due to the magnetic field perturbation. In contrast, spin--orbit coupling also induces current densities in the preceding ground-state calculation and the DFT framework needs to be generalized to a current density functional theory (CDFT) for consistency with the current-dependent response equations. Herein, we present the two-component relativistic generalization of the current-dependent kinetic-energy density of a Kramers-restricted Kohn--Sham reference for meta-GGAs and local hybrid functionals in NMR calculations. The extension is invariant under a position-dependent phase and a position-dependent spin rotation of the spinors, or a local U(1)$\times$SU(2) transformation. Relativistic effects are considered with exact two-component theory using a superposition of atomic potentials to include the two-electron picture-change correction (SAP-X2C).

papers.title: CaLA: Causal Latent Adjustment for World Models under Adaptive Policies
CrossCheck I: Cost Bounds of Imperative Programs as Constrained Optimization, with a Sound Cost Logic and a Verified Certificate Checker
Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense
Enhancing Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with Feed-Forward Priors via Spectral Fusion and Distillation
Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
papers.abstract: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $\epsilon_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $\alpha^2(36\pi^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192\pi^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $\alpha = (4/9\pi)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

papers.title: Disjointness, Orthogonality and Commutativity in $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: We characterize order-theoretic disjointness of two elements $a$ and $b$ in the self-adjoint part of a $C^*$-algebra $A$ via the condition $aAb = \{0\}$ and the trivial intersection of closed two-sided ideals generated by $a$ and $b$. As a consequence, we show that disjoint complements coincide with the self-adjoint parts of annihilator ideals. We also prove that $A$ is commutative whenever every pair of algebraically orthogonal positive contractions in $A$ is disjoint. Finally, we establish corresponding commutativity criteria involving projections for real rank zero $C^*$-algebras.

papers.title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
Moiré-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
papers.abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

papers.title: Supersymmetry of Helmholtz waves
papers.abstract: Symmetry organizes physical laws, links conservation principles to transformations, and reveals connections between seemingly different systems. We show that Helmholtz waves support Witten supersymmetry through their spatial symmetries, without additional internal degrees of freedom. Reflection across the transverse horizontal axis induces a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ grading of the Euclidean algebra, whose odd generators supply charges connecting opposite-parity Cartesian and Bessel modes at equal separation eigenvalues. The Bessel model has an unpaired even zero mode, Witten index one, and unbroken supersymmetry for any rotation-axis position along the reflection line. We express all four separators through mixed supercommutators of displaced orbital-angular-momentum generators, establish Weber pairing through a spectral sign operator, and identify the obstruction to equal-eigenvalue Mathieu pairing at nonzero ellipticity. We extend our construction to multiple transverse shells and generate supersymmetric partner fields with a common Talbot recurrence. Gaussian apodization centered on the rotation axis gives finite-power fields and preserves our charge relations during exact forward propagation while modifying the ideal revival. Our framework may guide optical transformations between parity partners and the characterization of structured fields.

papers.title: Decision Models for Definition-Driven GitHub Actions Workflow Smell Detection
Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
papers.abstract: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.

papers.title: A New Population of Jovian Exoplanets Suitable For Direct Imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, the Roman Coronagraph, and ELTs Identified from HARPS Radial-Velocity Data and Hipparcos-Gaia Astrometry
papers.abstract: We jointly analyze archival radial-velocity data from the HARPS spectrograph and astrometry from Hipparcos and Gaia to identify and constrain the dynamical properties of new and known long-period jovian exoplanets. Our search yields 14 new confirmed planets with masses of 0.04--6.1 $M_{\rm Jup}$ and semimajor axes of 0.1--12.6 au. Planets include a super-Jupiter in a near-Saturn-like orbit producing a strong astrometric acceleration (HIP 669 b), an eccentric Jupiter around a K star with a modest acceleration (HIP 39039 b), a 74-day-orbit warm Neptune (HIP 64550 b), and a giant planet around a Tier A Habitable Worlds Observatory target that may endanger any habitable zone Earth (HIP 17378 b). Three systems show evidence for candidate planets requiring additional data for confirmation. Our modeling also constrains the dynamical masses and orbits for 32 previously known radial-velocity-discovered planets. Orbits, masses, and ages for our sample show that five targets are potentially detectable in reflected light with the Roman Coronagraph, 28 should be imageable in reflected light with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, and six may be detectable in thermal emission with E-ELT/METIS. These results demonstrate the power of combining archival radial-velocity data with astrometry to discover and characterize long-period giant planets, a capability that will only grow with Gaia DR4. It provides a new sample of targets for future direct-imaging observations, and shows a path forward for timely vetting of targets for exo-Earth imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

papers.title: A Meta-analysis of Chemical Abundances Derived from Ultraviolet and Optical Lines of Os, Ir, and Pt, and a Reassessment of the Robustness of the Third r-process Peak in Metal-poor Stars
papers.abstract: We reassess the abundance ratio between elements at the third rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) peak (Os, Ir, Pt) and the lanthanide element Eu. We show that some weak optical lines of Os I, Ir I, and Pt I yield abundances inconsistent with stronger ultraviolet (UV) and optical lines and provide recommendations for their limited use alongside more reliable lines. We perform a meta-analysis of Os, Ir, and Pt abundances from 35 studies of 77 r-process-enhanced metal-poor stars spanning -3.43 < [Fe/H] < -1.27 and +0.22 < [Eu/Fe] < +2.45. The mean third-peak to lanthanide abundance ratios are $\log\varepsilon$(Os/Eu) = 0.86 $\pm$ 0.02, $\log\varepsilon$(Ir/Eu) = 0.88 $\pm$ 0.03, and $\log\varepsilon$(Pt/Eu) = 1.12 $\pm$ 0.04, which agree with the inferred Solar System r-process ratios to within 0.05 dex. These abundance ratios vary by less than 0.50 dex (a factor of 3.2), 0.56 dex (a factor of 3.6), and 0.45 dex (a factor of 2.8), respectively, in 90 percent of the r-process events that enriched metal-poor stars in existing samples. We use a representative r-process model to show that the small range of stellar abundance ratios favor models with a substantial contribution from neutron-rich material, with electron fractions, $Y_e$, < 0.2. We conclude that the third-peak to lanthanide abundance ratios are robust in existing r-process-enhanced star samples. In two stars with [Eu/Fe] < 0, the upper limits derived from non-detection of Pt indicate that the third-peak elements are deficient relative to lanthanides, and we conclude that this may be a signature of the limited r-process.

papers.title: A spin chain as a deformed conformal field theory: an ODE/IM approach
papers.abstract: The ODE/IM correspondence relates ordinary differential equations to integrable quantum field theories in the continuum. We ask whether it extends to integrable spin chains of finite length $N$. We analyse the twisted XXZ chain at a special anisotropy and twist, focusing on states in its Lee--Yang scaling sector. Their finite-size corrections are expected to come from the Lee--Yang conformal field theory deformed by irrelevant operators, and with the help of the ODE/IM correspondence we make this deformation explicit for the energy and the local conserved charges. Near each of the two edges of the distribution of the Bethe roots, the chain behaves as one chirality of the Lee--Yang theory in a generalised Gibbs ensemble, whose chemical potentials depend on $N$. The ODE/IM correspondence describes each of these ensembles by a cubic oscillator, whose coefficients we determine as series in $1/N$. The two chiralities are not independent: finite-size effects couple them, so that the charges of each shift the chemical potentials of the other. This turns out to be a generalised $T\bar T$-type interaction. Solving this coupling self-consistently, we obtain the energy and the local conserved charges of the chain as series in $1/N$, with no free parameters. We verify these series against the Bethe ansatz, for the ground state and for an excited state.

papers.title: Localization and homogenization of anisotropic fractional energies
papers.abstract: We study the joint limit of localization ($s\uparrow1$) and periodic homogenization ($\varepsilon\downarrow0$) for anisotropic fractional energies with $p$-growth and oscillating kernels. We prove that the $\Gamma$-limit is governed by the single parameter $\theta=\lim\varepsilon^{p(1-s)}$, and that its density is the convex combination $\theta\mathcal{A}^* + (1-\theta)\bar{\mathcal{A}}$ of the homogenized and the averaged densities. This shows that the picture recently obtained for quadratic energies also holds for every $p$ and for anisotropic kernels, with no regularity in the oscillating variable; the approach is different, and is based on convex duality. A nonlocal version of the duality argument gives the limit as $s\uparrow 1$ for a fixed kernel under weak assumptions, correcting a previous proof by the authors.

papers.title: The SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping Project: Time-delayed Variability of a Quasar's C IV Broad Absorption Troughs
papers.abstract: Broad absorption line (BAL) quasars offer a powerful view into the structure, kinematics, and feedback mechanics of active galactic nuclei. In this study, we track the dramatic behavior of intrinsic CIV outflows of the quasar SDSS J142129.40+522752.0 at z = 3.228. We analyze 199 high-signal- to-noise optical spectra collected over a 12-year baseline via the Sloan Digital Sky Survey III/IV Reverberation Mapping and the SDSS-V Black Hole Mapper Reverberation Mapping programs. We quantify multi-year variability across two prominent absorption features: a primary high-velocity CIV BAL trough (Trough A) and a lower-velocity mini-BAL (Trough B). Both troughs exhibit rapid, significant variations in equivalent width and average depth, culminating in temporary disappearances during the 2022-2023 observing seasons before reappearing at their original velocities. We find that the behavior of the two troughs is highly correlated with both the g-band flux and each other, strongly indicating that the observed variability is driven by ionization state changes of the gas. The equivalent width of the mini-BAL Trough B is found to lag that of Trough A by ~4 days in the quasar rest frame, suggesting that the equilibrium timescales of the two absorbers are different and possibly indicative of different outflow densities or distances.

papers.title: Flat Space Entanglement from Wedge Holography
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in three-dimensional flat space by combining wedge holography with a controlled flat limit of AdS end-of-the-world branes. The limit takes a wedge of AdS$_4$ bounded by two AdS$_3$ branes to a Randall-Sundrum-like configuration of two flat branes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval in the two-dimensional corner CFT becomes that of an interval at null infinity of the branes. The result has the functional form of the entanglement entropy of a two-dimensional Carrollian CFT, the proposed holographic dual of gravity in asymptotically flat three-dimensional spacetimes. However, the inferred central charges yield $c_M=0$ and $c_L\to\infty$ in the flat limit. Adding a gravitational Chern-Simons term produces a $c_M$-like contribution, but we still find $c_L\to\infty$ and $c_M\to0$ in this limit. Moreover, the corresponding extremal surfaces do not approach the swing surfaces proposed by Song and collaborators. Instead, they collapse onto null rays along null infinity. We argue that both features are generic for flat limits of AdS/CFT. They follow from entanglement entropy being a property of the domain of dependence and from the equality of causal and entanglement wedges for intervals in the vacuum.

papers.title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
papers.abstract: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

papers.title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
papers.abstract: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $\Psi$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$\Psi$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

papers.title: Parallel and perpendicular: a two-population test with POSSUM radio galaxies confirms hint of CMB birefringence
papers.abstract: Analyses of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarisation find an isotropic rotation of the linear polarisation plane, cosmic birefringence, of $\beta\sim0.2^\circ$--$0.3^\circ$, hinting at parity-violating physics. An independent test at low redshift with different systematics is needed. Radio galaxies provide such a test because their Faraday de-rotated polarisation angle $\chi_0$ is statistically aligned with their position angle $\psi$. Previous tests fitted only the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx90^\circ$. We add the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx0^\circ$, which is rotated by the same angle. We fit $\chi_0-\psi$ with two axial von-Mises distributions plus a uniform background, with an unbinned likelihood including each source's angle error. We apply this to 33,298 components of 16,649 double radio sources from the Polarisation Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM), with both components at polarised S/N $>10$ and separated by more than half the beam. Both populations are equally abundant. In the CMB convention we measure $\beta=0.48^\circ\pm0.35^\circ$, agreeing with the CMB in sign and amplitude. Including the $0^\circ$ population halves the variance of $\beta$. Components closer than half a beam carry no information on the source axis; excluding them leaves $\beta$ unchanged and makes the two populations consistent in all morphological classes. Combining with the joint ACT and Planck likelihood for a late-time rotation yields $\beta=0.282^\circ\pm0.056^\circ$, $5.0\sigma$ from zero. At $z\sim0.5$, radio galaxies probe the rotation of the last $\sim$ 5 Gyr. A CMB-sized rotation there would point to a late-evolving field such as axion-like dark energy, whereas a rotation before reionisation, e.g. by axion-like dark matter, predicts $\beta\approx0$. Given absolute angle calibration, the full POSSUM survey can test the CMB result independently.

papers.title: Exotic Portals for Hadronic Processes: The Gluon-Gluon and Gluon-Quark Portals
papers.abstract: In this work we explore all possible light exotic (LEX) particles which are accessible through the gluon-gluon ($g$-$g$) and gluon-quark ($g$-$q$) phenomenological portals up to effective dimension six. We present effective models for these new states, which are directly accessible through gluon and quark fusion processes, and which are guaranteed decays involving Standard Model (SM) quarks and gluons. We note many accessible states in particularly unusual SU(3)$_\text{c}$ representations, which contain large Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. We also include some interesting dimension seven operators with highly unusual features. We also consider all potential spin values for our LEX states, looking at Lorentz representations and color selection rules.
