In this, we find that states in various unusual Lorentz representations are accessible. We also find that certain operator types have restrictions on allowed color representations based on spin.

papers.title: RSK with a twist, mirabolic Steinberg variety, and Pak--Postnikov representations
papers.abstract: There is a beautiful interplay between the classical Robinson--Schensted correspondence and the Steinberg variety, which is the union of conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V)$. The irreducible components of the Steinberg variety gives the geometric interpretation of RS, and Pak--Postnikov description of RS as U,D operators is the combinatorics shadow of the $S_n\times S_n$-representation inside the top homology of the Steinberg variety. We study the conormal components of $Fl(V) \times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$, where $L(\lambda)$ is an irreducible representation of $GL(V)$. We show that there are only three families of $L(\lambda)$ such that $Fl(V)\times Fl(V) \times L(\lambda)$ has finitely many orbits. These families are determinant twists of classical RS, Travkin's mirabolic RSK and its Fourier dual. We extend the combinatorial interpretation of RS in terms of U,D operators to mirabolic RSK. Finally, we give a filtration of the top homology of the mirabolic Steinberg variety in which each graded piece is a Pak--Postnikov $S_n \times S_n$-representations.

papers.title: From residuals to warps: Probing disk geometry with gas kinematics
papers.abstract: Evidence of shadowing among protoplanetary disks suggests that warped protoplanetary disks are widespread, making it crucial to constrain their three-dimensional shape in order to understand their dynamical evolution and origin. Yet, inferring this warp shape from observations is challenging, as the typical signatures of a warp, especially shadows, are often degenerate with the warp shape. Kinematics of disks may provide a method to recover the shape by interpreting the residuals from a Keplerian disk model as local changes in inclination and position angle. In this work, we test its applicability and limitations. We perform radiative transfer simulations of disks with a parametrized warp shape to create synthetic maps of $^{12}\mathrm{CO}$ rotational line emission at ALMA wavelengths and compare the fitted warp with the true warp shape. We find that the warp shape can be recovered for nearly face-on disks with small warp misalignments of a few degrees, even without knowledge about disk properties such as emission height. The overall warp shape remains traceable even at moderate spectral resolutions up to $0.8\,\mathrm{km/s}$. However, we identify regimes where the method breaks down, including disks with an inclination higher than $40^\circ$, a high emission height of the tracer, and sharp warp transitions. In addition, radial and vertical motions can introduce apparent warps and twists, motivating extensions of the method to account for these effects.

papers.title: Analysis and Optimal Approximation of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations with Unbounded Control Operators
Revisiting TOI-2120 b: Updated mass and radius constraints on a sub-Neptune orbiting an M4 dwarf
papers.abstract: We present updated mass and radius measurements of TOI-2120 b, a short-period (5.80 days) planet orbiting a mid-M dwarf identified by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). TOI-2120 b was previously validated through transit photometry and high-resolution imaging, with a radius near the upper boundary of the radius valley around low-mass stars. We refined the planetary properties by combining archival TESS and ground-based photometry with new transit observations from the ARC 3.5m and Red Buttes Observatory (RBO) telescopes and new precision RV measurements obtained with the Habitable-zone Planet Finder (HPF) spectrograph. Our joint analysis yields a radius of $2.31\pm0.7$ Rearth, larger than previously reported. We also measure a planetary mass of $5.81^{+2.94}_{-2.69}$ Mearth at 2$\sigma$, corresponding to a bulk density of $2.62^{+1.37}_{-1.22}$ g cm$^{-3}$, positioning TOI-2120 b toward the water-rich region predicted by isocomposition models. Additional RV observations will be needed to further constrain its mass and composition.

papers.title: Elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model via the Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double
papers.abstract: We construct the Hamiltonian structure of the elliptic spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider model with dynamical inhomogeneities by Poisson reduction of the affine Heisenberg double extended by an affine oscillator manifold. This construction extends the Heisenberg double approach to spin Ruijsenaars--Schneider models from the hyperbolic to the elliptic case. We solve the moment map constraint and derive the Poisson algebras of the invariant Lax operator and spin variables. A realization with finitely many degrees of freedom is obtained by evaluating and localizing the invariant oscillators at distinct points of the affine parameter. Consistency requires these points to be dynamical so that their nontrivial Poisson brackets with the spin variables cancel derivative terms that would otherwise obstruct closure of the Poisson bracket on finitely many degrees of freedom. The resulting Poisson brackets and Hamiltonian coincide with those recently obtained from the elliptic Coulomb branch of the necklace quiver. Our construction thus provides an independent derivation of this Hamiltonian structure and establishes a direct link between Poisson reductions and Coulomb branches.

papers.title: Three-phase contact lines as distinct molecular adsorption environments
papers.abstract: In wetting and multiphase systems, three-phase contact lines form where liquid, solid, and gas phases meet, creating effectively one-dimensional boundaries with distinct molecular environments. Despite their ubiquity in droplets, liquid menisci, capillary bridges, porous materials, and confined multiphase systems, molecular adsorption at these lower-dimensional boundaries has remained largely unexplored. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to show that the contact line on a hydrophobic substrate is not merely the geometric intersection of two interfaces but a distinct thermodynamic adsorption environment with a substantially stronger affinity for amphiphilic molecules than either neighboring interface. The investigated amphiphiles of different molecular structures exhibit a common scaling relation between line and surface adsorption in the dilute regime, while their behavior becomes molecule-specific at higher concentrations. Furthermore, contact-line affinity increases exponentially with alkyl-chain length, leading to crowding at progressively lower concentrations and making contact lines extraordinarily sensitive to trace amphiphilic impurities. Because line, surface, and bulk populations scale differently with system size, contact-line adsorption becomes increasingly important at small length scales, where it can substantially alter molecular partitioning. Contact-line enrichment is predicted to reduce the line tension by an amount comparable to its intrinsic magnitude, with potentially substantial consequences for heterogeneous nucleation. Our results establish molecular adsorption as a fundamental property of three-phase contact lines with implications for wetting and multiphase systems across length scales.

papers.title: OmniX: A first jet and event model
A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver for Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo
papers.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation can reduce the number of evaluations needed to estimate an average, but its advantage in PDE uncertainty quantification depends on the cost of each coherent solve. We study this problem for incompressible Brinkman flow through a porous material with spatially varying drag. We first express the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map, obtaining a positive-definite system that preserves incompressibility in the exact formulation. We then introduce a Sobolev--Riesz preconditioner and prove that the resulting condition number is bounded by $\alpha_{\max}/\alpha_{\min}$, independently of the grid resolution. We construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for this formulation and show how to estimate the mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field. By accounting for both sampling and solver costs, we establish conditions under which the method has a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers. Numerical experiments verify the conditioning bound and the accuracy of the circuit components at the tested sizes. The complexity advantage is conditional on the stated input and discretization assumptions; no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.

papers.title: Nuclear deep-inelastic scattering as a BSM probe via SMEFT
papers.abstract: Searches for New Physics at the energy frontier have motivated theoretical development of model-independent methods to constrain interactions beyond the Standard Model (BSM) like the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), as well as associated phenomenological analyses. While these approaches are powerful, they are also afflicted by the large space of higher-dimensional operators and the challenge of possible degeneracies among these operators. To help ameliorate these difficulties, processes beyond those at hadron colliders, including deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), have been identified and studied for their ability to contribute added constraining power. In this work, we extend such investigations to charged-lepton DIS involving heavy nuclei, for which we explore the systematics of SMEFT effects for a series of representative cases. In particular, we point out that nuclear effects can reshuffle the luminosities governing partons entering SMEFT-corrected hard interactions, such that the nucleus can serve as an expanded laboratory to explore SMEFT effects complementary to free-nucleon DIS. In particular, we find that nuclear DIS possesses significant constraining power over flavor-isovector SMEFT operator combinations, with reduced nPDF dependence; similarly, improved control over nPDFs would further enhance the SMEFT reach of nuclear DIS observables. We explore projections for future (proposed) facilities like the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh, finding that improvements to nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) can further sharpen the reach of nuclear DIS.

papers.title: Bayesian approach to the Student's t-test based on the B-FBST
papers.abstract: This article proposes an exact Bayesian formulation of the B-FBST Student's t-test applied to the one-sample Student's t-test. The method relies on constructing an exact posterior distribution of the standardized parameter, then calculating the e-value to measure the evidence against the null hypothesis. To improve the stability of the procedure, posterior densities obtained from bootstrap samples are aggregated using random weights. A Monte Carlo simulation study was then conducted to compare the B-FBST Student's t-test with the classical Student's t-test and the bootstrap Student's t-test. The results, obtained from 100 Monte Carlo replications and 200 bootstrap replications, show that the B-FBST Student's t-test exhibits favorable overall performance, with an average of 71.0% correct decisions, compared to 65.5% for the classical test and 70.7% for the bootstrap test. The proposed method thus appears to be a robust alternative, particularly in several situations where the classical assumptions of the Student's t-test are compromised.

papers.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.

papers.title: Refined Rényi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
papers.abstract: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their Rényi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined Rényi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined Rényi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.

papers.title: CoRe: Jointly Learning Contextual Representations for Understanding and Generation
Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
papers.abstract: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.

papers.title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
papers.abstract: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

papers.title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
papers.abstract: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $\chi^{-4/3}$, where $\chi$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.

papers.title: When heavy vectors meet top partners: HVTP, a unified framework for composite Higgs searches
Look Where Camouflage Breaks: Concealment-Guided Observation for Camouflaged Object Detection
Circulating currents around orbifolded defects
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic monodromy defects with five dimensional orbifold singularities which lift to smooth and supersymmetric ten dimensional geometries. Such geometries have been of recent interest in spindle compactifications and have been interpreted as generalized Gukov-Witten defects. They are constructed by taking an orbifold of previously considered holographic monodromy defects on a space with a conical excess angle, and are not adiabatically connected to the empty anti-de Sitter vacuum. The the orbifold action acts nontrivially both on the five dimensional base as well as the five-sphere. We calculate one-point functions and anomaly coefficients as a function of the monodromies and orbifold data. Surprisingly, we discover that defects exhibit nonzero circulating currents even when all monodromies are turned off, unlike defects adiabatically connected to the vacuum, and therefore correspond to 1/8-BPS excited states. Comparing defects with nontrivial bulk topology we find that the A-type anomaly coefficient is always larger than those with trivial topology, while the B-type coefficient can be either larger or smaller.

papers.title: Counting elliptic curves by discriminant
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|\Delta_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - \delta}$ for any fixed $\delta > 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.

papers.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
papers.abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}\sigma$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

papers.title: Charge-resolved four-lepton probes of an $eμ$-flavour-violating scalar at FCC-ee
The hot circumgalactic medium: implications of mixing and resolution at the disk-halo interface
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that microphysical processes at the disk--halo interface, typically unresolved in circumgalactic medium (CGM) simulations, strongly affect the thermodynamic structure and observational signatures of an inflowing hot ($\sim10^6\,{\rm K}$) CGM. If the hot gas is pulled through the interface faster than it can cool, e.g.\ by turbulent mixing with the ISM or fountain flows, the hot CGM approaches an isentropic state. If instead the interface is regulated by radiative cooling on the hot gas cooling time, the hot CGM develops an outward-increasing entropy profile akin to a classic cooling flow. The two regimes differ by a factor of $\sim\!10$ in the predicted hot gas density above the disk near the rotation axis, and consequently by a factor of $\sim100$ in the predicted X-ray emission measure. We show that an isentropic CGM is produced in idealized CGM simulations that fail to resolve the pc-scale disk--halo interface, as numerical mixing drives artificially rapid cooling at the interface. A similar isentropic structure is found along the rotation axis in FIRE zoom-in simulations of $z\sim0$ Milky-Way-mass galaxies, where the cooling layer is likewise unresolved, raising the possibility that numerical mixing contributes to the isentropic structure. In contrast, an outward-increasing entropy profile forms in our idealized simulations when we replace the unresolved interface with an inner boundary that enforces a slow inflow. This outward-increasing entropy profile is likely also present in the Milky Way hot CGM, inferred from comparing density estimates at $\sim100\,{\rm kpc}$ with the entropy of the eROSITA bubbles.

papers.title: Probing the X-Ray Structure of the $z = 2.38$ Strongly Lensed Quasar J1721+8842, the First Einstein Zig-Zag Lens, Down to $140\ \mathrm{pc}$
papers.abstract: Sub-kiloparsec X-ray structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN), including outflows, jets, and dual AGN, provide key insights into their evolution and influence on host galaxies. In the local universe, Chandra X-ray Observatory's state-of-the-art $0.5''$ angular resolution has resolved these structures, but at $z > 0.1$, milliarcsecond resolution is required to spatially resolve sub-kpc scales. We leverage the spatial amplification by strong gravitational lensing to investigate the X-ray structure of J1721+8842, a $z=2.38$ quasar lensed into six images. To reconstruct the optical emission position, we model the lensing mass distribution using the six quasar images, five detected by Gaia Data Release 3 (A-E) and one by HST (F). Our model reproduces the five Gaia image positions to milliarcsecond precision. To locate the X-ray emission relative to the optical, we combine ray-trace simulations of archival Chandra observations with the lens model image position predictions using a double maximum-likelihood analysis. We constrain the X-ray centroid within a $0.017''\times0.004''\ (139\times30\ \mathrm{pc})$ ellipse centered $0.005''\ (44\ \mathrm{pc})$ away from the optical source position. Source-plane reconstructions of the soft-X-ray and hard-X-ray to optical sources demonstrate these emission regions are cospatial, allowing the optical source at $1\sigma$ confidence. These results indicate no evidence for kpc-scale X-ray jets, outflows, or dual AGN with projected separations exceeding $140\ \mathrm{pc}$. This method improves Chandra's effective angular resolution by a factor of 30 at cosmological distances, enabling studies of sub-kpc AGN X-ray structure at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Euclid: Discovery of a quasar at z = 8.13 hosting a 360-million-solar-mass black hole
papers.abstract: Quasars powered by rapid accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have been uncovered deep into the first gigayear of cosmic history. We present the discovery of EUCL J150452.291+625224.39 (J1504+6252), selected from Euclid Wide Survey imaging and spectroscopically confirmed as the first quasar at z > 8 through observations with Keck, HST, LBT, and JWST. J1504+6252 exhibits the defining spectral signatures of archetypal quasars at lower redshift, including a luminous blue power-law continuum and broad permitted emission lines, indicating a classical broad-line region. JWST/NIRSpec G395M spectroscopy yields a systemic redshift of z = 8.129 +/- 0.005, corresponding to 630 Myr after the Big Bang and shifting the quasar redshift frontier by about 39 Myr (6% of the age of the Universe at that epoch). From H-beta and Mg II, we measured intrinsic broad-line-region FWHM of 3160 +/- 270 and 3740 (+160/-170) km/s, respectively. A widely used single-epoch H-beta calibration gives a reference black hole mass of log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.56 +/- 0.43. Applying a range of calibrations to both Mg II and H-beta yields log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.33-8.89 and Eddington ratios of 0.12-0.44. Assembling a black hole of several hundred million solar masses within the first few hundred million years, despite its currently sub-Eddington accretion rate, requires either a massive seed or sustained, highly efficient early growth. The discovery of a mature, sub-Eddington quasar at z > 8 suggests that substantially more luminous quasars hosting similarly massive black holes may remain to be discovered. Conversely, previously known reionisation-era quasars may represent the rapidly accreting end of a broader population of already massive black holes spanning a wider range of accretion states.

papers.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
papers.abstract: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

papers.title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
papers.abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

papers.title: Low-excitation molecular gas in a Ly$α$-associated companion of the $z=4.7$ quasar in BR1202-0725
authors: Centre de Recherche Astrophysique de Lyon UMR5574
(9) School of Astronomy and Space Science
(10) Key Laboratory of Modern Astronomy and Astrophysics (Nanjing University)
papers.abstract: Quasar companions at high redshifts are usually gas-rich star-forming galaxies whose molecular gas masses ($M_{\mathrm{mol}}$) are estimated from [C II], dust emission or a single mid-$J$ CO line. We detect CO(5-4) and [C I](1-0) with ALMA in LAE-2, a Ly$\alpha$-associated companion of the $z=4.7$ quasar in BR1202-0725, and CO(5-4) at the location near LAE-1, the Ly$\alpha$ emitter between the quasar and the submillimeter galaxy (SMG). With the CO(2-1) flux from the literature, LAE-2 has an $L'_{\mathrm{CO(5-4)}}/L'_{\mathrm{CO(2-1)}}$ ratio of $0.22\pm0.04$, as in high-redshift main-sequence galaxies but four times lower than in the quasar host and the SMG. A non-LTE model places the CO(5-4) excitation temperature only 4 K above the cosmic microwave background (CMB), yet the same gas would show an even lower ratio against the $z=0$ CMB. The CMB-corrected $M_{\mathrm{mol}}$ from [C I], $\approx9\times10^{10} M_{\odot}$, agrees with the independent [C II] estimate, whereas CO(5-4) gives a four times lower mass if assumed thermalized at 40 K with the same CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor. Combining our 3 mm measurement with archival far-infrared photometry, we find cold ($\approx25$ K) dust and main-sequence star formation, with a gas-to-stellar mass ratio of $\approx4$ and a depletion time of $\approx0.7$ Gyr. Its star formation can supply the far-ultraviolet field that the [C I], [C II], and CO lines require. Quasar companions can thus retain massive, weakly excited molecular gas reservoirs that mid-$J$ CO surveys can miss.

papers.title: How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation
papers.abstract: Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. On the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall and with the particle crossing the light ring. Finally, we investigate how much of the signal is sourced from the strong-field region by switching off the source at some finite radius. The resulting waveform is exponentially close -- in cutoff radius -- to that of a standard infall. These results provide insight into the dependence of QNM excitation on the properties and dynamics of the perturbation, and offer a controlled setting in which to investigate the origin of black hole ringdown.

papers.title: Quantum State Preparation from Nonreversible Markov Chains via Spectral Filtering
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for preparing and transporting coherent quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains. Our approach uses spectral filtering to construct state-dependent phase operations, which are combined with fixed-point amplitude amplification to transport quantum states along a sequence of related chains. We study two complementary constructions with different oracle requirements and target states. The first uses coherent access to both forward and time-reversed transitions and targets the stationary quantum sample, with a filtering cost governed by a multiplicative-reversibilization gap. The second requires only forward transitions and selects the leading eigenstate of a flat discriminant, which may differ from the stationary quantum sample; we quantify this bias under additional spectral and reversibility-on-average conditions. For the forward-only construction, we implement the spectral filter using generalized quantum signal processing with a single signal qubit, apart from transition registers and oracle workspace. We establish a common transport procedure and derive error and resource bounds that account for spectral properties, overlaps between successive selected states, and the costs of coherent multi-step transition oracles. Up to logarithmic factors, spectral-filter degrees scale inversely with the square roots of the relevant spectral gaps, while transport introduces an additional inverse-square-root dependence on certified lower bounds on squared overlaps between successive selected states. Our results extend existing nonreversible spectral methods to multistage coherent state transport with controlled approximation errors.

papers.title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

papers.title: Casimir Experiments as Spin-Force Detectors
A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
papers.abstract: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.

papers.title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.

papers.title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
papers.abstract: Entanglement and magic are usually regarded as independent quantum resources. Here we connect the two in the toric code, where the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored logical state, a widely used measure of magic, acquires a direct interpretation in terms of entanglement. We introduce the spinal reflected entropy, defined on a neighborhood of a spine of the underlying surface as the reflected entropy between a disk around the vertex of the spine and bands along its noncontractible loops. It obeys an area law with a topological correction and contains one additional term that carries all the dependence on the stored state. On a torus, this term equals the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored state plus the logarithm of the ground-state degeneracy. The mechanism is topological. On the surface sewn to its reflected copy, the bands close into tubes, logical Pauli operators become anyon charges threading them, and these charges are distributed as the outcomes of Bell sampling of the stored state. The result extends to surfaces of higher genus and to general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes on qubits. Logical magic thus becomes a geometrically defined entanglement quantity, one that shallow circuits preserving the code space cannot change.

papers.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
papers.abstract: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $\Lambda$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

papers.title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
Bootstrapping two-loop $β$-functions for bosonic and heterotic strings
papers.abstract: Beyond one loop, $\beta$-functions of non-linear $\sigma$-models are hard to compute directly. We obtain them instead as a gradient flow of the low-energy effective action, whose coupling-space metric is fixed exclusively by symmetry. This gives a two-parameter family of O$(d,d)$-covariant, two-loop $\beta$-functions that covers the bosonic and heterotic string at once. Because only symmetry enters, the method opens a route to higher loops. As an application, we derive the two-loop RG flow of the integrable $\eta$- and $\lambda$-deformations; for the heterotic string, the correction is half of the bosonic one.

papers.title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
papers.abstract: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\sim\Delta^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

papers.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
papers.abstract: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

papers.title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
papers.abstract: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.

papers.title: Dark vector meson effects on composite dark matter
papers.abstract: We extend previous studies of $\mathcal{G}$-parity-odd dark pion dark matter in a QCD-like $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$ gauge theory with electroweakly interacting dark quarks to include the effects of $\rho$ mesons. We show that vector mesons can substantially affect relic abundance calculations through resonant enhancement, significantly affecting the conditions required to reproduce the observed relic abundance. Electroweak interactions further induce mixing between the dark $\rho$ mesons and Standard Model gauge bosons, opening new decay channels for the dark $\rho$ and modifying the effective interactions of the dark pions. We recast existing ATLAS and CMS searches to constrain the model, and perform a collider phenomenology study targeting the future FCC-hh and muon colliders, focusing on the resonant enhancement of cross sections in the $e^+e^-$, $\mu^+\mu^-$, and $W^+W^-$ final states for the latter. We show that the FCC-hh could probe $\rho$ mesons whose mass is up to 40 TeV.

papers.title: AGN feedback in the multiphase inner intracluster medium of a cosmological super-resolved galaxy cluster
papers.abstract: The intracluster medium (ICM) of galaxy cluster cores is a multiphase environment regulated by active galactic nuclei (AGN) feedback. Extended cool gas nebulae with complex morphologies and kinematics are commonly observed in cool-core clusters, but their origin and interaction with AGN feedback remain poorly understood. We present a cosmological magnetohydrodynamical zoom-in simulation of a low-mass cool-core galaxy cluster ($M_{\mathrm{200c}}=2.3\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$), using initial conditions from TNG-Cluster and the IllustrisTNG galaxy formation model. Through super-Lagrangian refinement, we achieve a baryonic mass resolution of $2.3\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and a spatial resolution of $\sim40\text{-}90$ pc in the cool ($10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}<T<10^{5.5}\,\mathrm{K}$) gas phase within the central $370$ ckpc, while retaining the full cosmological context. We investigate the properties and evolution of cool clouds and filaments and their interaction with AGN feedback at $z\leq0.35$. The cluster core hosts a rich population of dense, low-entropy filaments, including inflowing and outflowing structures and occasional rotationally supported disks. Comparing simulations with AGN kinetic feedback turned off and on, we find that AGN activity fragments and redistributes the cool gas and increases its covering fraction without destroying the cool gas reservoir. Individual outbursts drive transient increases in the velocities and velocity dispersions of both cool and hot gas, on short, $\lesssim 50$ Myr, timescales. We also identify low-entropy gas uplifted by AGN-driven outflows. While feedback globally heats the ICM and offsets cooling, it also creates conditions that may favor local thermal instabilities -- through shock compressions, mixing, turbulence, and uplift.

papers.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
papers.abstract: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $\pi$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

papers.title: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causality
papers.abstract: Indefinite causal order allows processes in which the order of events is not predetermined, enabling information-processing advantages unattainable with fixed causal structures. A long-standing open problem is whether such processes can be certified without trusting the devices used to demonstrate them, analogous to device-independent certifications of Bell nonlocality. Causal inequalities offer a route towards this goal, since their violation is intended to rule out all definite causal structures. However, fully device-independent certification of indefinite causal order remains elusive. The difficulty lies in the closed laboratories assumption, which requires each party to interact at most once with systems that mediate communication. Without this assumption, ordinary two-way communication can reproduce causal-inequality violations without involving indefinite causal order. Yet an untrusted device could violate the assumption by interacting with the mediating system more than once, while remaining undetected from input-output statistics alone. We address this loophole by embedding a minimal set of additional experimental components into a certification scheme. These elements probabilistically probe the underlying process, enabling the closed laboratories assumption to be validated directly within the protocol. Our framework provides operationally meaningful minimal-assumption tests of indefinite causal order, clarifying its distinction from nonlocality and paving the way for cryptographic and self-testing applications.

papers.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
papers.abstract: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

papers.title: Refining the Architecture of the Quadruple Pre-main-sequence System HD 98800: Improved Orbits, Dynamical Masses, and a Transiting Circumbinary Disk
papers.abstract: We present new spectroscopic and interferometric observations of the pre-main-sequence hierarchical quadruple system HD 98800, a member of the nearby TW Hya association. Our radial velocity monitoring extends the total coverage to over 36 years, sampling the periastron passage in the $\sim$240-yr outer orbit. By combining these velocities with new and archival interferometric observations of both inner binaries (A and B), we significantly refine the system orbits and constrain the dynamical masses of all four stars to $\leq$ 2.6 percent. The resulting stellar properties (masses, effective temperatures, and absolute magnitudes) are found to agree well with current stellar evolution models. Notably, binary B hosts a known circumbinary disk in a polar orientation. Our interferometric imaging, as well as ground-based photometry by others, capture binary A currently passing directly behind the disk, a striking alignment given the outer orbit's long period. We use the photometry to infer the optical extinction produced by the disk material. The eclipse is expected to last about a decade, and offers an unprecedented opportunity to probe the structure and composition of the potentially planet-forming disk. Our refined orbits and component masses provide a robust dynamical framework to support ongoing and future studies of this unique event.

papers.title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
papers.abstract: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

papers.title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($\mu$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $\mu$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $\mu$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.

papers.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
papers.abstract: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

papers.title: Superdaisy Resummation in Theories with Broken Gauge Symmetries
papers.abstract: We extend the partial dressing resummation scheme for the finite-temperature effective potential to the gauge and ghost sectors of spontaneously broken gauge theories and apply the resulting framework to the Standard Model. Going beyond the usual high-temperature treatment, we retain the full mass dependence of the thermal self-energies and determine the scalar, gauge-boson and ghost masses self-consistently from a coupled system of gap equations. The solutions show that corrections beyond the leading $\mathcal{O}(T^2)$ approximation are particularly relevant for the gauge-boson thermal masses, while they induce a comparatively small shift in the scalar spectrum for the benchmark studied. The self-consistent gauge-boson dressing in the longitudinal sector reduces the barrier in the finite-temperature Higgs effective potential. Implementing the resummation in the transverse sector removes the barrier and would seem to exclude a first-order phase transition in accordance with lattice results. While such resummation is not quantitatively reliable, due to the transverse excitations becoming strongly coupled, the results showcase the crucial role played by transverse modes in determining the nature of the electroweak phase transition.

papers.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
orbitize! v4: Joint Orbit Fitting with Gaia DR4 Astrometry and Flexible Analytic Linear Marginalization
papers.abstract: orbitize! is a Python package for Bayesian orbit fitting of planetary and stellar companions (Blunt et al., 2020). It provides a unified framework for fitting relative astrometry, radial velocities, and absolute astrometry, supporting analyses of both resolved and unresolved systems. Available posterior sampling methods include parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) through ptemcee (Foreman-Mackey et al., 2013; Vousden et al., 2016) and nested sampling through dynesty (Speagle, 2020), nautilus (Lange, 2023), and pymultinest (Buchner et al., 2014; Feroz et al., 2019). This paper accompanies the release of orbitize! version 4.0 and describes the functionality added since version 3.0 (Blunt et al., 2024), with a particular focus on joint orbit fitting with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry and the implementation of the Orbits for the Extremely Impatient (OFTeI) algorithm (Blunt et al. 2026b, in preparation).

papers.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).

papers.title: JWST/NIRSpec observations of AMORE6 suggest active Pop~III star formation in a self-polluted galaxy
papers.abstract: AMORE6 is a strongly lensed ($\mu\simeq78$), intrinsically faint galaxy at $z=5.725$, previously proposed as a metal-free candidate from the absence of [OIII]$\lambda$5007 in NIRCam slitless spectroscopy. We present deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy of its brighter image, AMORE6-B. We detect HeII$\lambda\lambda$1640,4686, with HeII$\lambda$4686/H$\beta=0.080\pm0.015$ and EW(HeII$\lambda$4686)$=35\pm8$ Å, weak [OIII] ($R_3=0.25$) and CIV$\lambda\lambda$1548,51, and no other metal lines. H and He lines give negligible attenuation, $T_e\simeq2\times10^4$ K, and $Y=0.226^{+0.022}_{-0.024}$. The oxygen abundance, $12+\log(O/H)\simeq6.08^{+0.24}_{-0.80}$ (0.04-0.4% $Z_\odot$, depending on the calibration), is the lowest at its stellar mass, while C/O is near or above solar. Photoionization models of different ionizing sources favour metal-free stars with a top-heavy initial mass function (IMF), as in the self-polluted phase of simulated Population III (Pop III) galaxies, or a metal-poor population with a luminous hard X-ray source; ordinary metal-poor populations, very massive stars, and accretion-based sources are disfavoured. A full SED fit in the fiducial self-polluted scenario gives $1.3\times10^5\,M_\odot$ of Pop III stars formed within the last 4 Myr, which ionize mildly enriched gas and leak 86% of their ionizing photons. The HeII-to-Balmer ratio constrains the slope $x$ and characteristic mass $M_{ch}$ of the Pop III IMF jointly, to $90x-268\lesssim M_{ch}/M_\odot\lesssim172x-330$ ($3\sigma$; $M_{ch}\lesssim70\,M_\odot$ for a Salpeter slope), excluding the most top-heavy IMFs allowed by near-field constraints. X-ray binaries are a possible alternative, but require either a metal-poor population too young (1 Myr) to host compact objects and an X-ray luminosity far above that of metal-poor galaxies, or $2\times10^6\,M_\odot$ of older Pop III.2 stars whose metals were mostly expelled.

papers.title: Detecting Harmful Short Videos in Toxic Diet Culture: A Governance-Ready Evidence Framework with Sparse Autoencoders
Exact reconstruction of running vacuum cosmology in torsion and nonmetricity gravity
papers.abstract: Running vacuum cosmology provides a dynamical description of vacuum energy while retaining the strict equation of state $w_{\rm DE}=-1$. However, whether its complete cosmological dynamics can emerge from a gravitational Lagrangian remains an important theoretical question. In this work, we investigate this possibility within torsion and nonmetricity gravity, considering minimally coupled, nonminimal matter-coupled, and trace-coupled theories. We first reconstruct analytically the running vacuum energy density in $f(T)$ and $f(Q)$ gravity, showing that energy density matching does not generally imply identical equations of state or expansion histories. We quantify these differences using Pantheon+, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 BAO data. However, considering trace-coupled $f(T,\mathcal{T})$ and $f(Q,\mathcal{T})$ gravity we extract explicit gravitational Lagrangians that exactly reproduce the complete running vacuum dynamics at the background level, namely both Friedmann equations, the strict vacuum equation of state, the matter-vacuum interaction, and the resulting expansion history. Furthermore, we identify regular solutions approaching a future de Sitter attractor, with positive matter and vacuum densities. Our results establish an explicit gravitational realization of running vacuum cosmology, extending beyond the mere matching of its effective vacuum energy density.

papers.title: Spectroscopic identification of z>7 quasars with Roman Space Telescope
papers.abstract: The Roman Wide Field Instrument grism will cover a large area over 1.0-1.93 micrometers, making it possible to search directly for Lyman-alpha breaks in quasars beyond redshift z = 7. We simulate quasars at z = 7.5-10 under HLWAS-like exposures with ESpRESSO, including PSF convolution, slitless dispersion, source and background Poisson noise, read noise, and Horne optimal extraction. Three Lyman-alpha equivalent-width (EW) prescriptions are used to bracket the uncertainty in line strength, and the extracted spectra are compared with M/L/T dwarfs and passive red galaxies using the spectral angle mapper. The Lyman-alpha-break completeness remains above 90% to J_AB approximately 23.7-24.1 and reaches 50% at J_AB approximately 24.3-24.7. Beyond J_AB approximately 25, the result depends strongly on the adopted EW distribution. In the fixed-redshift SAM test, the QSO recovery rate is TPR >= 0.982. None of the noisy brown-dwarf or red-galaxy test spectra is classified as a QSO. Because those test spectra are generated from the same finite parent libraries as the reference classes, this result measures the stability of the classification against noise within those libraries rather than an independently calibrated survey false-positive rate. At the faint end, the strongest astrophysical sensitivity in the present calculation is to the high-EW tail of the Lyman-alpha distribution.

papers.title: Fuzzy vectors from first and second moments: Affine consistency, carrying and sparsest realizations
papers.abstract: When the probability law of a random vector cannot be identified, its mean and possibly singular covariance can often still be elicited. We consider fuzzy vectors with compact convex cuts as mathematically tractable representations of such a moment pair, and ask how they must be designed to rely only on this information. We postulate two modeling desiderata, independence of the choice of origin and basis, and invariance under embeddings into a higher-dimensional space. Under these requirements alone we show that, in every ambient dimension, every level set of the fuzzy vector must be a Mahalanobis ellipsoid centered at the mean. Its complete specification then amounts to the choice of a radial profile for each covariance rank. We call a fuzzy vector a carrier of the moment pair if at least one of its random-set selections has exactly the given mean and covariance. For an ellipsoidal fuzzy vector of rank $p\ge1$ with radial profile $\rho$, carrying is equivalent to $\int_0^1\rho(\alpha)^2d\alpha\ge p$, and equality characterizes the inclusion-minimal carriers within the fixed-shape Mahalanobis class. A discrete random vector with the same mean and covariance and the fewest equally weighted atoms has its atoms on a regular simplex in Mahalanobis coordinates. Completing this simplex under the rotations left free by the moments yields the minimum-volume crisp ellipsoid in the state space that carries them. The ellipsoidal representation also encodes interaction through the covariance matrix.

papers.title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
Rupture and far-field profiles for Hénon-type MEMS elliptic equation with pressure
papers.abstract: Motivated by membrane touchdown in electrostatic microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) under external pressure, we study the Hénon-type elliptic equation $\Delta u=\lambda|x|^{\alpha}u^{-p}+F$, $u>0$, where $N\ge2$, $\lambda,p>0$, $\alpha>-2$, $F\in\mathbb R$, and $\alpha<2p$ if $F\ne0$. Near the origin, we construct positive radial rupture solutions with $u(0)=0$ for $F\ne0$ and infinitely many non-radial but asymptotically radial ones for every $F$, and derive expansions to arbitrary order. On exterior domains $\Omega_{R_0}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:|x|>R_0\}$, with no condition at the origin, we establish existence and uniqueness of positive solutions on $[R_0,\infty)$ for radial initial value problems with $u(R_0)>0$ if $p\ge1$, or if $F\ge0$ and $u'(R_0)\ge0$. We determine the leading behavior of all positive radial exterior solutions as $|x|\to\infty$ for $F>0$ and $F=0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$ and $\alpha\ge0$. For possibly non-radial exterior solutions satisfying $u(r,\theta)=A_\infty r^{\sigma_\infty}(1+o(1))$ uniformly in $\theta$, with $A_\infty>0$ and $\sigma_\infty\in\mathbb R$, we uniquely determine the leading exponent and coefficient in all three pressure regimes, without derivative bounds on the remainder. Although pressure affects only higher-order terms near an asymptotically radial rupture point, its sign changes the leading-order behavior at infinity under the stated hypotheses. Local radial rupture solutions extend uniquely to $\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}$ for $F>0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$, with the classified far-field profiles under the corresponding hypotheses.

papers.title: Flavor Alignment and Operator Sensitivity in a Left--Right Universal-Seesaw Model
papers.abstract: We analyse the flavour structure and low-energy operator sensitivity of a parity-related doublet universal-seesaw model with an imposed lepton triality. Degenerate bare singlet masses permit a basis in which light-light tree neutral flavour transitions vanish; the physical heavy masses remain nondegenerate. We connect this alignment property to the axial and scalar differences measured by $B_{d,s}^0\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and reproduce the six-state charged-vector mixing amplitudes for five reference masses. The reference analysis identifies kaon CP violation as the more sensitive flavour probe. Historical kaon data disfavour the lower reference masses, while estimates suggest that dimuon and radiative $B$-decay effects are harder to resolve at present precision. These comparisons use the specified reference spectrum and historical inputs. We also compare charged and neutral resonance rates with published search benchmarks. The vacuum hierarchy entails a cancellation of about $5\times10^{-6}$ at $M_{W_R}=80\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The initially thermal Dirac-neutrino branch has a dataset-dependent extra-radiation tension, strengthened in an illustrative mass-dependent decoupling estimate. For dimuon decays we establish operator selection rules and sensitivity estimates. The numerical flavour results cover meson mixing and charged-vector dipoles. We give no dimuon branching-fraction prediction or global allowed region.

papers.title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
Beyond Static Charts: Benchmarking Interactive Chart-to-Code Generation for MLLMs
Query Obfuscation with Embedding-Optimized Noise (EON): A Representational Blindspot in Agentic Retrieval
Exact Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphic Shear Splitting: Continuous-Discrete Geometric Bounds, Reversible Memory Backpropagation, and Expressivity Frontiers in Volumetric Mapping
Idempotent generically stable measures in NSOP$_1$ groups
papers.abstract: We prove the Idempotent Measure Conjecture for type-definable groups in theories whose Keisler randomization is NSOP$_1$. More precisely, every global idempotent frequency interpretation measure on such a group is the unique left-invariant and the unique right-invariant measure concentrating on its type-definable stabilizer. In particular, its support is a left-simple convolution semigroup and has a unique minimal left ideal. The announced theorem of Ben Yaacov, Chernikov and Ramsey that randomization preserves NSOP$_1$ (proof in the appendix) yields the corresponding conclusion for all type-definable groups in NSOP$_1$ theories.

papers.title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport
papers.abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

papers.title: What time is it in Assembly Space? Cronin and Walker's "The Physics of Causation" fails elementary dimensional analysis (Comment on arXiv:2601.00515)
papers.abstract: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.

papers.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
Products and duality for framed 1-flow categories
papers.abstract: We describe a product between framed 1-flow categories and show that it satisfies the expected Cartan formula on its second Steenrod squares. We also describe a dual framed 1-flow category and show that, like the Spanier-Whitehead dual of spectra, the homology groups of a framed 1-flow category can be shown to be isomorphic to the cohomology groups of its dual and that this isomorphism can be shown to cooperate with the framed 1-flow category structure in a suitable sense.

papers.title: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
papers.abstract: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual affine formulas with integer coefficients on residue classes. The same finite-state method extends four numerical tables of Zhang. We also give the entire augmented sequence for $c>\max S$ when the losing heaps of $S$ are exactly the multiples of a fixed integer.

papers.title: High Throughput Meets Low Latency: CKKS Functional Bootstrapping on GPUs
Turbulent Epidemics: Scale-dependent Fluctuations as a Probe of Population Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous dynamics, including phenomena such as superspreading and clustering, is a hallmark of many infectious diseases. A key challenge lies in identifying observables that constrain heterogeneous dynamics. We here adapt the technique of turbulence decomposition from fluid dynamics to extract scale-dependent fluctuation spectra and correlation functions from disaggregated epidemiological data as a probe of population heterogeneity. To investigate possible explanations for the observed heterogeneities during the COVID-19 winter wave in Germany in 2020/21, we calculate synthetic observables using the new network-based simulation code \textsc{Epimetheus} for an idealized structured population. The code can flexibly incorporate clustering, heterogeneous connectivity and susceptibility, superspreading as well as temporal modulations of transmission risk and factors like waning of immunity and vaccination. A qualitative comparison of simulated and observed fluctuation spectra and correlation functions as well as the secondary attack rate and the overdispersion indicates that both clustering and variations of susceptibility across population substructures of all scales are required to produce the observed dynamics. Combined with heterogeneous connectivity, it is likely that self-limiting effects would have limited the winter outbreak to $0.2\texttt{-}0.35$ of the population without further behavioral changes after the autumn of 2020. A uniform population-wide reduction of transmission risk alone does not adequately explain the observed heterogeneities. Further analysis of the relative contributions and interplay of interventions and self-limiting effects on COVID-19 disease dynamics is required. We outline avenues towards a better integration of heterogeneity in models for predicting infectious disease dynamics and diagnosing effects of interventions.

papers.title: Fusion Gains Depend on the Implementation and the Calibration Target: An 18-Task Study of Prediction Intervals with a Single-Source Fallback
Massless neutrinos in a left-right symmetric universe
papers.abstract: This comment is a comment stimulated by the 1957 Goldhaber et al. experiment, that detected a massless left-handed electron neutrino with negative helicity. The standard description of this neutrino is by means of a Weyl spinor. It is shown below that this description is incomplete, and in fact one needs a massless Dirac spinor to comply with the requirements of quantum field theory. A Dirac spinor is composed of two Weyl spinors. This in turn raises the necessity to explain the fate of the right-handed electron neutrino, partner of the Goldhaber et al. experiment's one. A possible explanation for its invisibility is suggested here in terms of a left-right symmetric extension of the standard model.
